references.text: Here Zelophehad is mentioned, son of Hepher, who had no sons, only daughters. The names of the daughters are listed: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah and Tirzah - the same names as in Joshua 17:3.

The daughters of Zelophehad come before Moses and demand inheritance rights because their father died without sons. This is the original account of their claim to inheritance which Joshua 17:3 refers back to.

This text concerns the marriage rules for the daughters of Zelophehad to ensure that the inheritance remains within the tribe of Manasseh. The daughters are named and marry within their father's tribe.
The continuation of the story where the daughters of Zelophehad come before the priest Eleazar and Joshua to claim their inheritance, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
Machir, son of Manasseh, is mentioned here as the father of Gilead - the same lineage traced back from Zelophehad in Joshua 17:3.
